topic_title: AI Dashboard Audit: The Duplicate Order Trap
hook: This AI dashboard looks polished, but its total is wrong.
key_takeaways: Audit source data before creating charts.
Repeated IDs require review, not blind deletion.
Reconcile the clean total against the original and removed amount.

segments.spoken: This AI dashboard looks polished, but its total is wrong.
In this sample, one duplicated order turns twelve thousand into fifteen thousand.
Before asking AI for charts, ask it to audit the rows.
Check repeated order IDs, confirm the currency, and check the date range.
Review the duplicate, then rebuild from the cleaned data and reconcile the total with the source.
Now the chart looks good and the number checks out.
This is sample data, not client results.
Comment CHECK for the audit prompt and practice file, and follow for more practical AI builds!

demo_steps: Read seven sample rows: AED 15,000, including one exact duplicate order of AED 3,000.
Flag repeated order O-1003 and compare all fields.
Verify one order per row, AED currency and 1–6 October 2026 window.
Review the exact duplicate, retain six original orders, reconcile AED 15,000 minus AED 3,000 equals AED 12,000.
Build the dashboard using the checked six-row file.

prompts.title: Audit before charts
prompts.text: Audit this CSV before making a dashboard. Do not alter the original. First state the unit of a row and the date/currency assumptions. For this practice file, each row is a complete order, not a line item. Flag repeated order IDs and distinguish exact duplicate rows from conflicting records. Show row numbers and the amounts affected. Do not delete repeated IDs automatically: explain why an exact row is a duplicate and ask before changing real data. Never merge currencies or guess exchange rates. Check missing values, numeric parsing and the date window. For the included sample only, remove the exact duplicate after review, save cleaned-orders.csv and reconcile original total minus removed amount equals cleaned total. Produce an audit log and a simple dashboard from the cleaned file. Show currency, date range, row count and assumptions. If anything cannot be verified, say so. Keep real customer data private and use an approved tool.

resource_page.body_markdown: Practice on a fictional seven-row orders CSV. One exact duplicate inflates AED 12,000 to AED 15,000. Download the original, cleaned CSV, audit log, reproducible Python audit and local dashboard. Each row represents a complete order. Never delete repeated IDs blindly; real line-item data may repeat an order ID legitimately. Confirm currency and date range, preserve the original and reconcile totals. All numbers are illustrative, not client results. AI presenter.
